title: Cluster 03 DRILL: The Molecular Basis of Cancer, and Stem Cells
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 8 questions · 90 marks · 17 parts · one mark per minute, so 90 minutes · cumulative over Cluster 1, Cluster 2 and Book 2
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Eight questions, 90 marks, 90 minutes. Every learning outcome this cluster owns is still tested; the table below shows which question carries each one. The set used to run 166 marks. The saving came from folding the lifetime-supply question and the leukaemia question into the stem-cell question they both depend on, and from marking each part for the answer it actually asks for rather than for everything that could be said. No outcome was dropped to make the time.

Every stem is one or two sentences and every answer is long. No stem lists the axes to compare on, no stem tells you which option is wrong, and no stem contains its own answer. Six parts carry the real figure from the paper or chapter it came from, not a redrawing. Two multiple-choice parts only, Q6(a) and Q7(a), both sitting on a figure that does real work, and both requiring all four options to be justified or rejected with the exact feature that kills each wrong one.

Cumulative, so an earlier gap counts double. Q1(a) needs the growth factor receptor, the G protein switch and the phosphorylation cascade from Cluster 1 said cold, plus the whole mutation chain from Book 2. Q2(a) needs the G1/S regulation point from Cluster 2. Q4(b) needs ligand and receptor binding from Cluster 1. Q7(a) and Q8(a) need differential gene expression from Book 2. Q8(c) needs mitosis giving genetically identical daughters, run backwards. Say the gap out loud when you hit one; the transcript is the gap list.

What the marks reward. Every mutation answer starts at the gene and runs base sequence to amino acid sequence to three-dimensional conformation to protein function, because a scheme rejects the opening marking points where the answer starts at the amino acid and never mentions the DNA. Cancer answers run forwards from the mutation; two examiner comments penalise arguing back from the wild type. The lexicon is strict: allele not gene, long-term self-renewal not divides indefinitely, lymphoid stem cell not blood stem cell or adult stem cell, secondary tumours at distant sites or it is invasion and not metastasis, and rate of division against rate of cell loss rather than excessive or uncontrolled growth.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicates. Q1 the two routes from a proto-oncogene to an oncogene · Q2 loss of function set against gain in function, and what an inherited cancer allele actually is · Q3 multi-step development and the accumulation of mutations · Q4 angiogenesis and metastasis as what makes one tumour lethal · Q5 the causative factors · Q6 potency, totipotent against pluripotent against multipotent · Q7 the blood lineage, lymphoid against myeloid · Q8 what stem cells do normally, and the same property read as a leukaemia. No concept is the primary target of two questions.

Two errors in your own chapter are built into this drill, because both sit on distinctions the outcomes exist to test. Chapter 3.4 page 14 calls embryonic stem cells totipotent, claiming each cell of the early blastocyst is capable by itself of developing into a healthy individual. It is wrong; pages 8, 13 and 16 of the same chapter are right. Q6 is built so that believing page 14 gives the wrong answer twice. Chapter 3.4 page 11 says the myeloid progenitor cell can generate all the different types of blood cell. It cannot; it cannot make lymphocytes, and page 20 gets it right. Q7 is built so that believing page 11 gives the wrong answer. 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 3 opens on lymphoid stem cells, so that second one is live.

Why so much of this drill is figure-led. Data and figure interpretation is 33.5 per cent of the Book 3 corpus and 35.9 per cent of it is figure, table or micrograph led, rising to 45.9 per cent in the curated bank. Any drill for this Book that is mostly text-only is not modelling the exam.
